findings.title: How misconfigurations in virtual environments can lead to compromise
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky GERT analyzed two ransomware cases on ESXi and Proxmox environments, including a BlackNevas intrusion that began with ransomware activity on a Windows system in a virtualized domain controller segment. The PRTG Network Monitor deployment held broad access to the ESXi hosts and the same root password was reused across several nodes, letting the attacker connect over SSH, upload an `esx` binary, disable execInstalledOnly, and delete logs. The article details the 2025-10-19 host timeline and recommends isolating management systems and eliminating shared privileged credentials.

findings.title: Ransomware at the hypervisor layer: how attackers use ESXi and vCenter features for malicious purposes
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky GERT investigated an engagement in which an adversary destroyed an organization's virtualization estate over 10 days, targeting four ESXi hosts, every virtual machine on them, both vCenter Server Appliances, and all connected backup infrastructure, with ransom notes naming BlackNevas, first observed in November 2024. No virtualization-layer vulnerability was exploited; every action against ESXi ran through legitimate VMware management interfaces. The report also notes the September 2021 Babuk source code leak, including its ESXi version, and that at least ten subsequent ransomware families leveraged it alongside leaked LockBit Windows builds.

findings.title: ESXi ransomware needed no hypervisor flaw, Kaspersky says
findings.summary_md: tbreak summarized Kaspersky's finding that two ransomware attacks on ESXi in October 2025 and Proxmox in August 2026 needed no VM escape. In the BlackNevas case, a monitoring tool with broad access and a root password reused across several nodes let the attacker into ESXi over SSH, and ESXi's execInstalledOnly control was disabled after root access. The article notes patching alone is insufficient and recommends least-privilege administrative access.

findings.title: Kaspersky Finds Routine Admin Gaps Opened the Door to Ransomware in Virtualisation Cases
findings.summary_md: BrandIconImage reported Kaspersky GERT's finding that BlackNevas ransomware activity in an ESXi environment in October 2025 and The Gentlemen ransomware in a Proxmox environment in August 2026 both relied on weak administrative controls rather than hypervisor flaws. In the ESXi case, PRTG Network Monitor had broad host access, the same root password was reused across nodes, and the attacker uploaded an `esx` binary, disabled execInstalledOnly, and deleted logs. The post recommends isolating virtualization management systems and eliminating shared privileged credentials.
